body.statement: Every finite first-order formula over a real closed field with rational polynomial atoms, including arbitrary finite Boolean combinations and alternating universal and existential variable blocks, admits effective quantifier elimination: its truth is decidable when it is a sentence, and when it has free variables its solution set has an effectively computable quantifier-free semialgebraic description. Consequently, if a first-order formula uniquely specifies a point in each nonempty compact semialgebraic fiber, its graph is semialgebraic and effectively describable.

source.verbatim_statement: If, instead of having a single block of variables quantified by the same quantifier the given sentence has several blocks of variables with alternating quantifiers, the problem is called the general decision problem for the first order theory of the reals.

attestation.note: Verified 2026-09-09 against the Basu--Pollack--Roy JACM article PDF: §1.1 explicitly defines the general decision problem with several alternating quantifier blocks, and Theorem 1.3.1 gives an algorithm that transforms first-order formulas over real closed fields into equivalent quantifier-free formulas. The semialgebraic-selector consequence used here is derived by applying that output to the first-order graph formula for the unique lexicographic minimizer; compactness is supplied by the calling proof, not by the citation.
